what: Photo·card columns flow endlessly at .8px per frame (60fps), and when scrolling down, speed is added by that distance × .05 (up to 2 at a time) so they speed up as if pushed, then settle at .94× each frame. Scrolling up only removes the added speed and never flows backward. Each column can be given its own up or down direction so they flow in a staggered way, and with axis: x it becomes a horizontal band

options.gain: Speed added by multiplying scroll px, default .05
options.max: Max speed added per single scroll, default 2 (1 for the benefits card column)
options.decay: Number multiplied into the attached velocity every frame, default .94
options.dir: Per column, up · down (left · right if horizontal) separated by commas — ”down, up” makes the two columns stagger. Default is all up
options.axis: if x, horizontal bands (default y: vertical columns)
options.[data-fx-part=col]: Flowing column — put one set (first child) inside. A part attaches one more set (data-fx-part=clone)

from.where: index.html .ix-about__wrap (photo columns on both sides of the intro text — original aboutMarqueeSettings baseSpeed .8 · maxBoost 2 · boostDecay .94 · scrollSensitivity .05, both moving up) · .ix-benefits__col (two columns of benefit cards — maxBoost 1, left moves down · right moves up). Phone uses a horizontal strip moving only .8px (no boost)

note: scroll-boost-marquee raises and lowers a speed multiplier (1 to 4.5x) on a .3s·.8s curve, whereas this adds px speed and decays it every frame so it never runs backward when scrolling up — the feel differs, so it was extracted separately
